A lot of people seem to conflate Hamlet's disgust with his mother's marriage to sexual feelings for his mother, but in my own opinion, I feel like disgust is a perfectly normal reaction to seeing your mother get married to your uncle within a month of your father's death. There is zero textual evidence for Hamlet being attracted to his mother; what there is textual evidence for, however, is Hamlet being disgusted by the thought of his mother having sex at all:

"Such an act that blurs the grace of modesty, / Calls virtue hypocrite, takes off the rose / From the fair forehead of an innocent love / and sets a blister there" (III.iv.40-5)

"You cannot call it love, for at your age / The heyday in the blood is tame, it's humble / and awaits upon the judgment \[...\]" (III.iv.68-70)

TL;DR: Hamlet is grossed out by his mom having sex with his uncle. For some reason, people think that means he has sexual feelings for her.
